I have farmed these 6 mu in Quzhou for forty years. I know every patch of this soil. My husband and I are getting older — there are only the two of us now — so I cannot afford to waste labor or money on things that do not work. I have well irrigation, which means I am not at the mercy of the rainfall, but pumping costs money, so I water only when the crops truly need it.

This autumn, I will plant winter wheat on all 6 mu. I will use an improved variety like the ones my neighbors have been growing — they yield well and resist lodging. Before sowing, I will do rotary tillage to break up the stubble and level the field. I will spread compound fertilizer as a basal dose, then topdress with urea at the green-up and jointing stages. I will irrigate three times: once before winter to help the seedlings survive the cold, once at jointing in spring, and once at heading to fill the grain. I will spray herbicide early, and then spray twice more for aphids and rust — three pesticide applications in total. I expect about 1,000 jin of wheat per mu if the spring weather cooperates.

After harvesting the wheat in early June, I will immediately plant hybrid maize — Denghai 605 or something similar — using no-tillage directly into the wheat stubble. Everyone here does it this way now; it saves time, fuel, and my back. I will put down compound fertilizer at sowing and side-dress nitrogen when the plants are knee-high. I will irrigate twice: once around the big-trumpet stage and once during silking if the weather is dry. Two pesticide sprays will be enough — one for weeds and one for corn borers. On good years this maize gives me 1,100 jin per mu.
